title: ACID Properties & Transaction Guarantees
oneLiner: Four core guarantees (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) ensuring reliable relational transactions.
imagePrompt: Four quadrant diagram visualizing Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability

body.definition: ACID is a set of properties that guarantee database transactions are processed reliably: Atomicity (all-or-nothing), Consistency (state invariants), Isolation (concurrency control), and Durability (persistence on disk).
body.whyItMatters: Guarantees data integrity in the event of system crashes, hardware failures, power outages, and high-concurrency conflicting operations (e.g. balance transfers).
body.commonPitfall: Confusing ACID 'C' (Consistency = domain constraints like non-negative balance) with CAP theorem 'C' (Consistency = linearizability/single-copy view).
body.interviewAngle: Tested through isolation anomalies (dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantom reads) and write-ahead logging mechanisms.

quickChecks.question: What happens if a server loses power mid-transaction before COMMIT?
quickChecks.answer: On recovery, the database uses undo logs to roll back partial writes (Atomicity).

quickChecks.question: How is Durability achieved without synchronous B-Tree disk writes?
quickChecks.answer: By appending sequential records to the Write-Ahead Log (WAL) before acknowledging.

title: B+ Tree Indexing & Query Execution
oneLiner: Self-balancing multi-way search tree storing records in linked leaf pages for O(log n) point and range queries.
imagePrompt: B+ Tree structure with internal routing nodes and doubly linked sequential leaf nodes

body.definition: A B+ Tree is a self-balancing search tree where internal nodes store routing keys and all actual data pointers are kept in sorted leaf nodes linked sequentially for range scans.
body.whyItMatters: Maximizes disk block I/O efficiency with high fan-out (thousands of child pointers per 4KB/8KB page), keeping tree depth to 3-4 levels for billions of rows with O(log n) lookup.
body.commonPitfall: Violating the Leftmost Prefix Rule on composite indexes (e.g. querying WHERE created_at > '2026-01-01' skips idx_users_org_created entirely, requiring full table scan).
body.interviewAngle: Standard question on clustered vs secondary indexes, index selectivity, covering indexes, and explaining EXPLAIN ANALYZE plans.

quickChecks.question: Why do B+ trees keep all data in leaf nodes rather than internal nodes?
quickChecks.answer: Higher internal node fan-out reduces tree depth, minimizing disk I/O operations.

quickChecks.question: Why are B+ Tree leaf nodes doubly linked?
quickChecks.answer: To allow fast sequential forward and backward range scans without traversing tree roots.

title: MVCC & Transaction Isolation Levels
oneLiner: Concurrency control mechanism providing snapshot isolation without blocking concurrent readers and writers.
imagePrompt: MVCC version chain showing row creation and expiration transaction timestamps

body.definition: Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) maintains multiple physical versions of a data row, allowing transactions to read consistent point-in-time snapshots without acquiring shared read locks.
body.whyItMatters: Eliminates read-write locking contention: 'Readers do not block writers, and writers do not block readers.' Powers modern Postgres, MySQL InnoDB, and Oracle engines.
body.example:
-- Row Versioning tuple structure
-- (xmin: creation_tx_id, xmax: deletion_tx_id, payload)
-- Tx 100: INSERT -> (xmin=100, xmax=0, 'Active')
-- Tx 105: UPDATE -> (xmin=100, xmax=105, 'Active'), (xmin=105, xmax=0, 'Pending')
body.commonPitfall: Neglecting VACUUM / garbage collection, leading to table bloat as dead row tuples accumulate after heavy UPDATE/DELETE workloads.
body.interviewAngle: Tested via the 4 ANSI SQL isolation levels (Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable) and Write Skew anomalies.

quickChecks.question: What is a Dirty Read?
quickChecks.answer: Reading uncommitted modifications made by another concurrent transaction.

quickChecks.question: How does MVCC enable lock-free reads?
quickChecks.answer: By serving historical row versions visible to the transaction's snapshot timestamp.
